q: 1. The aggregate is said to be elongated when
options: its least dimension is three fifth of its mean dimension
its least dimension is equal its mean dimension
its length is equal to its mean dimension
its length is equal 1.8 times of its mean dimension
explain: As defined in this text, an aggregate particle is classified as elongated when its length exceeds 1.8 times its mean sieve dimension.

q: 2. An aggregate should
options: be of proper shape and size
be clean, hard and well graded
explain: A good aggregate must satisfy all these criteria — proper shape/size, cleanliness, hardness, good grading, and chemical stability — to ensure quality concrete.

q: 3. The value of bulk density of aggregate depends upon
explain: Bulk density is influenced jointly by particle size distribution/grading, particle shape (affecting packing), and the specific gravity of the aggregate material — hence all of these factors matter.

q: 4. An aggregate generally should not preferred for use in concrete is one which has the following surface texture
explain: A glossy surface texture provides poor bond between the aggregate and cement paste, hence such aggregates are not preferred for concrete.

q: 5. An aggregate which may contain some moisture in the pores but having dry surface is known as
explain: A 'dry' aggregate condition refers to particles that may retain some internal pore moisture but present a dry outer surface, distinct from the fully saturated-surface-dry or very dry states.

q: 6. The rock which is not calcareous, it is
explain: Laterite is an iron and aluminium rich residual rock and is not calcareous (does not contain calcium carbonate), unlike limestone, marl, and chalk.

q: 7. An aggregate having all the pores filled with water but having dry surface is called
explain: Saturated Surface Dry (SSD) condition is defined as the state where all internal pores are filled with water but the surface itself is free of surface moisture.

q: 8. The sum of percentage of all deleterious materials in the aggregate shall not exceed
explain: As per IS 383 guidelines referenced in the text, the total permissible limit for all deleterious materials combined in aggregate is restricted to 5%.

q: 9. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: in properly graded aggregates, bulk density is more
in single size aggregates, bulk density is least
in single size aggregates, bulk density is maximum
explain: Single size aggregates have more voids between particles (since there are no smaller particles to fill the gaps), resulting in the least, not maximum, bulk density; so this statement is incorrect.

q: 10. The resistance of an aggregate to compressive force is known as
explain: The aggregate crushing value test measures the resistance of aggregate to gradually applied compressive (crushing) load.

q: 11. The bulk density of aggregates, depends upon
explain: Bulk density of aggregates is influenced by particle shape, grading, and degree of compaction, hence all these factors are correct.

q: 12. The resistance of an aggregate to the effect of hydration of cement and weather is called
explain: Soundness refers to the ability of aggregate to resist volume changes caused by weathering action, temperature and moisture changes, and chemical reactions such as cement hydration.

q: 13. The maximum quantity of aggregate per 50 kg of cement should not exceed
explain: As per general guidelines, the total quantity of aggregate (fine plus coarse) used per 50kg bag of cement should not exceed about 450kg for good quality concrete.

q: 14. The bulk density of aggregates, is generally expressed as
explain: Bulk density of aggregates is conventionally expressed in kg/litre for practical field and laboratory measurement purposes.

q: 15. The resistance of an aggregate to wear is known as
explain: The abrasion value test (e.g., Los Angeles test) measures an aggregate's resistance to wear caused by rubbing/attrition.

q: 16. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: continuous grading is not necessary for obtaining a minimum of air voids
the omission of a certain size of aggregate is shown by straight horizontal line on the grading curve
the omission of a certain size of aggregate is shown by straight horizontal line on the grading curve
explain: The grading curve shows a horizontal straight-line segment when a particular size fraction is missing (gap grading), and continuous grading isn't essential for minimum voids; hence all of the above are correct.

q: 17. Bulking of sand is
options: increase in volume of sand due to presence of moisture upto certain extent
explain: Bulking is the apparent increase in volume of a given mass of sand caused by moisture films separating the particles, up to a certain moisture content.

q: 18. The type of aggregate of same nominal size, which contain less voids when compacted, are
explain: Rounded spherical aggregates pack more closely together, resulting in fewer voids compared to irregular or flaky shapes of the same nominal size.

q: 19. With the moisture content of 5 to 10% by weight, the bulking of sand is increased by
explain: At moisture contents in the 5-10% range, sand bulking reaches values on the order of 50% increase in volume as per standard bulking curves.

q: 20. The main requirement, which a ware-house should fulfill is that
options: its walls should be water proof masonry construction
it must have large number of windows
explain: A cement warehouse must protect stored cement from moisture, requiring both water-proof walls and a leak-proof roof (options a and b together).

q: 21. The term 'ware-house pack' means
options: pressure compaction of bags in lower layers
pressure exertion of bags on upper layers
explain: 'Warehouse pack' refers to the phenomenon where cement bags stored in lower layers get compacted due to the pressure of bags stacked above them.

q: 22. According to IS: 382-1963, a good aggregate should be
explain: As per IS: 382-1963, aggregates for concrete must be chemically inert, sufficiently strong, and hard and durable, satisfying all listed conditions.

q: 23. As compared to ordinary Portland cement, high alumina cement has
options: higher initial setting time but lower final setting time
lower initial setting time but higher final setting time
higher initial setting time and final setting time
lower initial setting time and final setting time
explain: High alumina cement is characterized by a longer initial setting time but a comparatively shorter final setting time than OPC, giving rapid strength gain once setting begins.

q: 24. In designing a ware-house, it is assumed that
options: each bag contains 50 kg of cement
floor area occupied by one bag of cement is 0.3 m2
height of each cement bag containing 35 liters of cement is 0.18 m
explain: Standard warehouse design assumptions include a 50kg bag weight, about 0.3m² floor area per bag, and about 0.18m height per bag containing roughly 35 liters, so all these hold together.

q: 25. An aggregate is known as cyclopean aggregate if its size is more than
explain: Aggregate larger than 75 mm in size is termed cyclopean aggregate, generally used in mass concrete works like dams.

q: 26. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: the maximum size of a coarse aggregate, is 75mm and minimum 4.75mm
the maximum size of a fine aggregate, is 4.75mm and minimum 0.075mm
the material having particles of size varying from 0.06mm to 0.002mm is known as slit
the material having particles of size less than 0.002mm, is known as clay
explain: All the given size classifications for coarse aggregate, fine aggregate, silt, and clay are correct according to standard particle size definitions.

q: 27. In order to obtain the best workability of concrete, the preferred shape of aggregate is
explain: Rounded aggregate has minimum surface area and least interlocking/friction, which gives the best workability for a given water-cement ratio.

q: 28. If the aggregates completely pass through a sieve of size 75mm and are retained on a sieve of size 60mm, the particular aggregate will be flaky if its minimum dimension is less than
explain: Mean size = (75+60)/2 = 67.5mm; flaky if least dimension < 3/5 × mean size = 0.6 × 67.5 ≈ 40.5mm.

q: 29. Bulking of sand is maximum if moisture content is about
explain: The bulking effect in sand is typically at its peak (maximum volume increase) at around 4% moisture content, before it decreases again as the sand becomes saturated.

q: 30. In Q. No. 70 the aggregates will be known as elongated aggregate if its length is not less than
explain: Elongated if length ≥ 1.8 × mean size = 1.8 × 67.5 = 121.5mm (using the thrice-mean-size type criterion referenced in these questions).

q: 31. Finer grinding of cement
options: affects only the early development of strength
explain: Finer grinding increases the surface area available for hydration, which speeds up early reaction and improves early strength development, without significantly changing the ultimate (long-term) strength.

q: 32. An aggregate is said to be flaky, if its least dimension is less than
explain: By definition, an aggregate is classified as flaky when its least dimension (thickness) is less than 3/5th (0.6 times) of its mean dimension.

q: 33. A flaky aggregate is said to be elongated if its length is
options: four times than the mean size
explain: A flaky aggregate is further classified as elongated when its length exceeds thrice the mean size of the particle.

q: 34. The minimum percentage of void in round aggregate is
explain: Round/spherical aggregates, being able to pack closely, exhibit a minimum void percentage of about 33% compared to irregular or angular shapes.

q: 35. The fineness modulus of fine aggregate is in the range of
explain: Fine aggregate (sand) typically has a fineness modulus in the range of about 2.0 to 3.5, differentiating it from coarse aggregate which has a much higher FM.

q: 36. The light weight aggregates may be obtained from
explain: Lightweight aggregates such as pumice and scoria are derived from volcanic sources, which contain porous, low-density material.

q: 37. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: sands obtained from pits, is washed to remove clay and silt
sands obtained from flooded pits, need not be washed before use
sea shore sands contain chloride which cause efflorescence
the chloride in sea shore sand and shingle may cause corrosion of reinforcement if the concrete is porous
explain: All statements about pit sand washing, flooded pit sand, and sea shore sand chloride effects (efflorescence, corrosion) are correct.

q: 38. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: sand stones may be defined into calcareous, siliceous and ferruginous sand stones
concrete using sand stones, cracks due to excessive shrinkage
very hard and close grained crystallized lime stones are suitable aggregates but provide low strength
broken bricks produce a concrete having good fire resisting qualities
explain: All the statements regarding sand stone types, shrinkage cracking, limestone strength, and broken brick fire resistance are correct.

q: 39. The construction joints in cement concrete
options: should be located where bending moment is large
should be located where shear force is large
should not be provided at the corners
should be spaced at a distance of 3 m part in case of huge structures
explain: Construction joints should be avoided at corners since these are critical stress concentration zones and joints there could weaken structural integrity.

q: 40. The bulk density of an aggregate does not depend upon
options: size and shape of the container
explain: Bulk density is a material property depending on aggregate size, shape, specific gravity, and grading — it does not depend on the size and shape of the measuring container.

q: 41. The most useless aggregate is, whose surface texture is
explain: A glossy surface texture prevents good bonding between the aggregate and the cement paste, making it the least useful/desirable aggregate surface type.

q: 42. The aggregate impact value of the aggregate used in
options: road pavement concrete is less than 30
explain: As per IS specifications, the aggregate impact value limits given for building concrete (<45), road pavement (<30), and runway concrete (<30) are all correct.

q: 43. The creep strains are
options: caused due to dead loads only
caused due to live loads only
explain: Creep is the time-dependent deformation of concrete under sustained/continued stress, which can result from both dead and live loads acting over time.

q: 44. The bulk density of aggregates depends upon its
explain: Bulk density of aggregates is influenced together by particle shape, grading (size distribution), and the degree of compaction achieved during placement.

q: 45. The void ratio of
options: single size coarse aggregate is roughly 0.45
explain: The void ratios given for single size coarse aggregate, graded coarse aggregate, and fine aggregate are all approximately correct as standard values.

q: 46. The effect of creep on modular ratio is
options: either to decrease or to increase it
explain: Creep effectively reduces the modulus of elasticity of concrete over time, which increases the modular ratio (Es/Ec) used in design.

q: 47. The aggregate containing moisture in pores and having its surface dry, is known as
explain: Saturated surface dry (SSD) aggregate is defined as aggregate whose pores are filled with moisture but whose surface is dry, neither absorbing nor contributing extra water to the mix.

q: 48. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: bulking of sand is caused due to formation of a thin film of surface moisture
fine sand bulks more than coarse sand
with 10% moisture content by weight, the bulking of sand is increased by 50%
the volume of fully saturated sand, is equal to the volume of dry and loose sand
explain: All statements regarding causes of bulking, fine sand bulking more, the 10% moisture bulking figure, and saturated sand volume equaling dry sand volume are correct.

q: 49. Which of the following cement is expected to have the highest compressive strength after 3 days
explain: High alumina cement gains strength extremely rapidly, reaching very high compressive strength values within just 1-3 days, higher than the other cement types listed.

q: 50. Log Angles machine is used to test the aggregate for
explain: The Los Angeles Abrasion testing machine is specifically used to determine the abrasion resistance (hardness) of aggregates.
